messages:
mira: quick heads-up — spun up a small pilot for acme-13b int8 on a mixed-fleet slice. did a shotgun sampling across summarization / instruction-following / multi-doc retrieval slices. seeing modest token-econ wins but a few quality regressions on 'long-absorb' summarization slice.
kevin: rough numbers?
mira: TL;DR: raw token cost down ~18% vs fp16 baseline, throughput up ~12% for our p50 workloads. but long-absorb ROUGE drops ~4 points; hallucination spike on prompt-primed examples.
juan: do you have per-slice p95 latency? that's often where product care.
mira: p95 (int8): 240ms, fp16: 230ms on same seq len distro. p50 int8 ~95ms -> p50 fp16 ~105ms (so faster median). so tail slightly worse.
sasha: interesting — median improvements but tail regression. could be KV cache handling or attention kernel fallback. any logs?
mira: pasted a minimal trace snippet:```
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] model_load acme-13b-int8 quantize=dynamic kernel=matmul_avx fallback=false
[2026-03-20T14:05:03Z] req id=abc123 slice=long-absorb token_count=1800 kv_cache_misses=12 ctx_evictions=0
[2026-03-20T14:05:03Z] p95_step_latency=7.2ms kernel_swap=true
```
kevin: kv_cache_misses=12 on long context is concerning. did you enable prefix caching / kvcache pooling?
mira: yes pool on, but int8 runtime had a different allocation path causing ~2x more memcpy at long seqs. i suspect the memcpy pattern is the tail.
ben: from a unit-econ lens — can you give cost per 1M tokens and delta vs existing prod 13b fp16? product is asking for quick guidance.
mira: rough bucketed cost: fp16 baseline: $420 / 1M tokens. int8 run (current): $345 / 1M tokens (-17.9%). if we smooth batching and reduce memcpy overhead, we estimate ~$310 / 1M (-26%).
juan: product/GTN question — which slices drop quality the most? is this acceptable for low-risk customers?
mira: high-risk slices: multi-doc abstractive + long-absorb. instruction-following for short prompts is fine. hallucination cases are mostly citations/fact-aggregation where token compression changes attention precision.
sasha: can we run quick A/B with hybrid routing? send short/interactive traffic to int8, long-absorb routing to fp16. quick flagging would avoid user-visible regressions.
kevin: agree. add a canary rule: if prompt tokens > 1024 route to fp16. do we have rollout automation?
ops-bot: rollout flag created: rollout/prime-int8-20260320. canary=5% rules=seq_len>1024->fp16; else int8. triggered by mira.
ben: sounds reasonable. for GTN deck, recommend: "int8 for interactive/short-turn, fp16 for long/absorptive tasks; expected cost savings 18-26% with guarded routing; QA required on multi-doc summarization." keep it concise.
mira: next steps i propose: 1) instrument memcpy hotspots & KV miss counters, 2) run targeted int8 microbench on long contexts with pinned memory, 3) run 10k example smoke test for hallucination signal, 4) enable canary routing.
juan: timeline?
mira: i can do 1+2 today, 3 overnight, 4 asap once ops-bot confirms canary.
sasha: i'll prep a short eval suite focusing on citation precision and multi-doc coherence to send to GTN.
kevin: one more ask — capture AUC of quality vs cost curve per slice so product can choose threshold. small script suggestion:```python
# sample pseudo
def score_slice(samples, model_variant):
    for s in samples:
        out = call_model(model_variant, s.prompt)
        yield quality_metric(out, s.ref)
```
aggregate to produce cost_vs_quality.csv
```
mira: noted. i'll attach the csv to the canary ticket after smokes.
ben: thanks team. product wants a 1-paragraph recommendation by EOD summarizing production-safe routing and estimated savings.
mira: i'll draft it and ping GTN.
kevin: thanks — ping if you need extra tokens or GPUs for the microbench.
mira: will do. ending thread to start runs. :rocket:
